lead: D-Wave / QBTS — Nvidia's quantum seal of approval
smaller: Tesla / TSLA — shorts are cashing in on the backlash
Hims & Hers / HIMS — is the compounded-drug boom over?
Gold / GLD — the record while bitcoin falls
why_lead: The 13 and 14 March editions already ran the D-Wave breakthrough as the lead and as a smaller trade, so the draft lead needed a changed story. Today's evidence supplies one: on 18 March Nvidia said it will build an accelerated quantum computing research center, and its first-ever Quantum Day put IonQ's executive chair on a panel with Nvidia's CEO, while Yahoo Finance and The Motley Fool asked on the same day whether Rigetti is a pump-and-dump stock and whether D-Wave is still a buy. QBTS closed at 10.80 after a 100.74% five-session move, the largest among the retail-favourite names in the card.

The reaction also changed. On 18 March Rigetti fell 8.06% and IonQ 9.03% against D-Wave's 3.40%, so the peers did not add to the validation on the day it was dated. The new lead is built on that split and on the Nvidia catalyst, not on the 13 March breakthrough essay.
why_smaller: Tesla returns with a changed story, not the dip essays of 10 and 12 March or the loyalty lead of 17 March. The new items are Electrek's 0% China financing and Kelley Blue Book's registration report on 17 March, and Business Insider's short-seller story and CBS's Las Vegas attack report on 18 March. The 36.37% 20-session fall is in the card.

Hims & Hers returns after its 17 March small with a regulatory break rather than the 2X-fund angle: Quartz reported on 18 March that the stock tumbled on an FDA warning about unapproved weight-loss drugs, and the card shows a 9.22% last-session fall and a 46.17% 20-session drop.

Gold is the non-equity trade, but this is a changed attention set rather than the 17 March gold-at-3,000 essay: a record for the second time in a week, Decrypt's gold-up, bitcoin-down headline, Barron's slump headline and the FOMO warnings are all dated 18 March, and the card shows gold up 3.11% over 20 sessions while bitcoin is down 1.93%.
considered_not_chosen: Robinhood (HOOD): the 18 March lead on the prediction-markets hub; the draft's FINRA settlement is a 10 March headline, so no development is new beyond the 18 March explainer, and the theme is not carried.

Palantir (PLTR): an 18 March headline says the shares surged 17% on a US$19M buyback, yet the card shows a 3.96% last-session fall and a 32.68% 20-session drop. A reversal case with thin attention, left for a later edition.
Nvidia (NVDA): the 18 March small covered the GTC keynote; its quantum move now sits inside the lead.
Affirm (AFRM): the Walmart-partner loss was the 18 March small; no new development.
Rocket Lab (RKLB): smalls on 11 and 18 March; no new development since the 18 March edition.
Joby (JOBY) and Archer (ACHR): the air-taxi theme was the 17 March Archer small; the Virgin Atlantic chatter of 16 March is the same theme.
Dogecoin (DOGE-USD): three smalls in March; Cathie Wood's memecoin call of 18 March is the same angle again.
Silver (SLV): the 7 March squeeze small; the 17 March shorting headline is a variant of the same squeeze.
Intel (INTC): the 14 March small on the new CEO.
Sangamo, Altimmune, USA Rare Earth and Bridger Aerospace: attention headlines, but no ticker in the card, so no price can be used.
Indian options curbs and retail losses in India: no instrument in the card.
